stem: A client is starting atorvastatin. Which liver-enzyme monitoring plan is consistent with current labeling?

options.A: Obtain liver enzymes every month for every client taking atorvastatin regardless of symptoms or prior results.
options.B: Avoid all liver-enzyme testing after atorvastatin is started because transaminase results do not contribute to medication-safety assessment.
options.C: Wait to obtain any baseline liver assessment until symptoms of hepatic injury develop after therapy has already begun.
options.D: Consider liver-enzyme testing before atorvastatin is started and repeat testing when clinically indicated rather than on a fixed monthly schedule.

rationale: The current DailyMed LIPITOR label states: consider liver-enzyme testing before initiation and when clinically indicated thereafter. It does not require fixed monthly testing for all patients. Therefore D is correct.
educational_objective: Know that atorvastatin labeling supports baseline consideration of liver-enzyme testing and repeat testing when clinically indicated rather than routine fixed monthly monitoring for every patient.
source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine official drug label
source_document_title: LIPITOR — atorvastatin calcium tablet, film coated
source_locator: Warnings and Precautions §5.3 Hepatic Dysfunction: consider liver enzyme testing before LIPITOR initiation and when clinically indicated thereafter; contraindicated in acute liver failure or decompensated cirrhosis.
source_claim_supported: Current LIPITOR labeling advises considering liver-enzyme testing before initiation and repeating testing when clinically indicated, not on a universal fixed monthly schedule.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: review pertinent data before medication administration, monitor medication response/adverse effects, and provide safe medication care.
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — statin monitoring and hepatic safety

source_original.stem: A client is starting atorvastatin. Which liver-enzyme monitoring plan is consistent with current labeling?

options.A: Obtain liver enzymes every month for all patients taking atorvastatin regardless of symptoms, risk factors, or previous results.
options.B: Avoid all liver-enzyme testing after atorvastatin is started because transaminase results do not contribute to medication-safety assessment.
options.C: Wait to obtain any baseline liver assessment until symptoms of hepatic injury develop after atorvastatin therapy has already begun.
options.D: Consider liver-enzyme testing before atorvastatin is started and repeat it when clinically indicated rather than following a fixed monthly schedule.

source_original.rationale: Atorvastatin labeling advises considering liver-enzyme testing before initiation and as clinically indicated thereafter.
source_original.source_detail: §5.3 Hepatic Dysfunction. DailyMed LIPITOR label revised 4/2024; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Overview of Content — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12: medication administration, controlled substances, adverse effects/interactions, monitoring and teaching. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the labeling-based monitoring construct and key D, confirmed the exact April 15, 2024 DailyMed label and §5.3 wording, shortened distractors, and reduced difficulty from hard to easy because the final item tests a direct label instruction.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current DailyMed LIPITOR label; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item reproduces the label's baseline/clinically-indicated testing approach without inventing routine monthly testing.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because the label does not require universal monthly testing.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because clinically indicated liver-enzyme testing remains relevant.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because testing may be considered before initiation.

audit_findings.cueing: All options address monitoring timing; D is not dependent on length or stylistic cueing.
audit_findings.blueprint: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication monitoring and adverse-effect prevention.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read the current LIPITOR label, §5.3 wording, all choices, rationale, objective and blueprint mapping. D remained uniquely correct.
